nodes.title: CORNING INCORPORATED SUPPLEMENTAL INVESTMENT PLAN (As Amended and Restated Effective January 1, 2023)
nodes.heading: Exhibit 10.40 CORNING INCORPORA TED SUPPLEMENT AL INVESTMENT PLAN (As Amended and Restated Effective January 1, 2023)
nodes.start_phrase: CORNING INCORPORA TED (the “Company”) hereby amends and restates in its entirety , effective January 1, 2023, the Corning Incorporated Supple mental Investment Plan (the “Plan”) to permit Eligible Employees to defer a portion of their compensation to supplement contributions they make pursuant to the Corning Incorporated Investment Plan.
nodes.summary:
This partial document is an amended and restated version of Corning Incorporated’s Supplemental Investment Plan, effective January 1, 2023. It allows eligible employees to defer a portion of their compensation to supplement contributions made to the Corning Incorporated Investment Plan. The restated terms apply to plan benefits earned or vested on or after January 1, 2005 under IRC Section 409A.

Article One provides key definitions:
- Board: the Board of Directors of Corning Incorporated.
- Change in Control: a 409A-compliant change in ownership or control, triggered by any of the following: (i) a third-party tender or exchange offer for Corning common stock; (ii) a person acquiring beneficial ownership of 50% or more of the combined voting power of outstanding securities; (iii) a contested election leading to a board majority turnover within 12 months; or (iv) a merger where Corning is not the survivor, a consolidation, a sale of all or substantially all assets, or an approved plan of partial or complete liquidation.
- Code: the Internal Revenue Code of 1986, as amended.

nodes.title: Definitions
nodes.heading:
ARTICLE ONE

Definitions
nodes.start_phrase: “Board” means the Board of Directors of Corning Incorporated.
nodes.summary:
- Document type and scope: Corning Incorporated Supplemental Investment Plan (SIP), Exhibit 10.40, amended and restated effective January 1, 2023; applies to benefits earned or vested on/after January 1, 2005 under Section 409A.
- Plan purpose and legal intent:
  - Provides eligible executives the ability to defer additional compensation and receive company contributions beyond limits of the Corning Incorporated Investment Plan.
  - Intended as an unfunded “top-hat” deferred compensation plan for a select group of management or highly compensated employees under ERISA Title I.
  - Designed to comply with Section 409A; supersedes inconsistent prior terms.
- Key definitions established (Article One), including:
  - Board; Committee (Compensation Committee or delegate); Company; Plan; Plan Year.
  - Effective Dates: original January 1, 1997; second restatement effective January 1, 2023.
  - Change in Control: must meet 409A definition and occurs upon (i) third-party tender/exchange offer, (ii) acquisition of ≥50% voting power, (iii) Board majority turnover from contested elections within 12 months, or (iv) merger where Corning is not survivor, consolidation, sale of substantially all assets, or shareholder-approved liquidation.
  - Compensation: includes base salary and specified cash bonuses (e.g., Division Cash Awards, Individual Outstanding Contributor Awards; GoalSharing and Performance Incentive Plan awards). Excludes company plan contributions, equity plan awards, non-cash bonuses, commissions, Corporate Performance Plan awards, stock purchase contract value, dividends/dividend equivalents, reimbursements, overseas/COLA allowances, death benefits, severance, signing bonuses, special achievement bonuses, and other unusual payments; Committee may add includable items.
  - Eligible Employee: employees of a Participating Company who meet eligibility in Section 3.1(a) and are approved by the Committee.
  - Participating Company and links to Pension Plan definition/approval.
  - Investment Plan (401(k)) and Pension Plan references.
  - Company Stock Fund: invested primarily in Corning common stock.
  - Section 409A and Trustee (potential rabbi trust).
- Eligibility and participation rules (Article Three excerpt):
  - Eligibility each Plan Year requires being on Company payroll and being in a Committee-designated select group of management or highly compensated employees; eligibility reassessed annually.
  - Participation begins per employee election (Section 4.3).
  - Base salary deferrals into the SIP commence only after Investment Plan contributions are suspended due to (a) hitting the 401(a)(17) compensation cap ($330,000 in 2023) or (b) reaching the 402(g)/414(v) contribution limits.

nodes.title: Purpose and Intent of Plan
nodes.heading:
ARTICLE TWO

Purpose and Intent of Plan
nodes.start_phrase: The purpose of this Plan is to attract and retain a highly-motivated executive workforce by providing to Eligible Employees the opportunity to defer additional Compensation and for the Company to make additional contributions on behalf of Eligible Employees in excess of those permitted under the Investment Plan.
nodes.summary:
- Defines “Section 409A” (Internal Revenue Code Section 409A and related guidance) and “Trustee” (a Board-designated trustee for a rabbi trust to pay Plan benefits).
- States the Plan’s purpose: to attract and retain executives by allowing additional compensation deferrals and Company contributions beyond limits of the Investment Plan.
- Clarifies the Plan is an unfunded deferred compensation plan for a select group of management or highly compensated employees under Title I of ERISA (a “top hat” plan).
- Affirms the Plan is intended to comply with Section 409A and will be interpreted accordingly.
- Provides a supremacy clause: this Plan’s terms override any other plans/documents with inconsistent or additional terms.
- Sets eligibility: for any Plan Year, an employee must be on Company payroll and designated by the Committee as part of the select management/highly compensated group.
- Notes eligibility is determined each Plan Year and does not automatically carry over to subsequent years.
- Outlines participation: begins per the employee’s election (referenced in Section 4.3); base salary deferrals start only after the employee’s Investment Plan contributions are suspended due to reaching the Code Section 401(a)(17) compensation limit ($330,000 in 2023) or after hitting the maximum contributions under Code Sections 402(g) and 414(v).

nodes.title: Eligibility and Participation
nodes.heading:
ARTICLE THREE

Eligibility and Participation
nodes.start_phrase: An employee shall be an Eligible Employee and be entitled to participate in this Plan during any Plan Year that (i) such employee is on the Company payroll for the Plan Year; and (ii) such employee belongs to a select group of management or highly- compensated employees as provided for in Title I of ERISA that the Committee has designated as being eligible to participate in the Plan.
nodes.summary:
- Defines “Section 409A” (Internal Revenue Code Section 409A and related guidance) and “Trustee” (a Board-designated trustee for a rabbi trust to pay benefits).
- States the Plan’s purpose: attract and retain executives by allowing additional compensation deferrals and Company contributions beyond the qualified “Investment Plan” limits.
- Clarifies plan status: an unfunded, nonqualified deferred compensation “top-hat” plan for a select group of management or highly compensated employees under ERISA Title I; intended to comply with Section 409A; supersedes inconsistent documents.
- Eligibility: each Plan Year, an employee must be on Company payroll and designated by the Committee as part of the select group to be an Eligible Employee; eligibility is reconsidered annually.
- Participation: begins per the employee’s deferral election (Section 4.3). Base salary deferrals start only after the employee’s Investment Plan contributions are suspended due to Code limits (401(a)(17) comp cap) or after reaching the 402(g)/414(v) elective deferral limits. Bonus deferrals follow the employee’s bonus-specific election.
- Employee contributions: pre-tax salary reductions; may defer up to the Investment Plan’s maximum contribution percentage; base pay and bonus deferrals are elected separately; base pay deferrals commence once qualified plan limits prevent further contributions.
- Company matching allocations on base salary deferrals: for deferrals that would have been matched under the Investment Plan, the Company credits a match in this Plan at the same level/terms as the Investment Plan, ignoring Code limits and counting this Plan’s elective deferrals as compensation for match calculations; non-Code-imposed plan caps on matching apply in aggregate across both plans.
- Special match rules effective January 1, 2023 for employees accruing the career average (Part I) Pension Plan benefit:
  - 24+ years of vesting service as of prior December 31: 100% match on base salary deferrals up to 5% of base pay.
  - Fewer than 24 years: 75% match on base salary deferrals up to 5% of base pay.

nodes.title: Contributions
nodes.heading:
ARTICLE FOUR

Contributions
nodes.start_phrase: An Eligible Emp loyee may contribute to this Plan in a Plan Year any amount of his or her Compensation durin g the Plan Year (not to exceed the maximum percentage of compensation permitted under the Investment Plan for employee contributions), in the amount set forth on the Eligible Employee’ s deferral election form.
nodes.summary:
- Article Four (Contributions)
  - Employee contributions:
    - Eligible Employees may elect to defer base salary and/or bonus on a pre-tax basis via salary reduction, up to the Investment Plan’s maximum percentage for employee contributions.
    - Base salary deferrals to this Plan begin only after contributions to the Investment Plan cease due to Code limits on compensation and/or contributions.
    - Bonus deferrals are permitted regardless of Code limits; all deferrals follow Section 4.3 election rules.
  - Company allocations:
    - Matching allocations:
      - Base salary and bonus deferrals are matched at the same level and terms as under the Investment Plan, ignoring Code limits on compensation and contributions and treating deferrals here as compensation for match purposes.
      - For Plan Years beginning on/after 1/1/2023, for employees accruing under the career average formula of the Company’s Pension Plan (part I):
        - With ≥24 years of vesting service as of prior Dec 31: 100% match up to 5% of base salary/bonus.
        - With <24 years of vesting service: 75% match up to 5% of base salary/bonus.
      - Any Investment Plan cap on Company match not attributable to Code limits applies in aggregate across both plans.
      - Maximum match requires contributing the required percentage from both base salary and bonus.
    - Allocations for long-service employees:
      - For those accruing under the career average Pension Plan formula who elect to contribute base salary or bonus: 1.175% of base salary for periods with base salary contributions, plus 1.175% of bonus compensation taken into account, provided a bonus contribution was made (otherwise zero for bonus).
    - Company allocations suspended:
      - No Company Allocations for compensation earned in payroll periods beginning May 25, 2020 through the payroll period ending December 20, 2020, and for contributions made from such compensation.
  - Deferral elections (Section 4.3):
    - Elections must be made by the last day of the prior Plan Year for compensation earned in the next year (including bonuses earned in that year but paid the following year).
    - Initial election specifies deferral amount and form of payment for retirement benefits; the form of payment elected in the first deferral applies to all subsequent deferrals. Elections are irrevocable for the applicable year; changes apply only prospectively to future years.
    - Separate, continuing elections for base salary and bonus; new elections become effective for compensation earned in the following Plan Year. “Base salary” and “bonus” are defined distinctly for election purposes.
    - Base salary deferrals require a simultaneous Investment Plan deferral election; deferrals to this Plan start only when Investment Plan contributions stop due to Code limits, and the Investment Plan deferral election is irrevocable for the Plan Year.
    - Bonus deferrals to this Plan occur regardless of Code limits; that bonus cannot be deferred into, nor count as compensation for elective or matching contributions under, the Investment Plan (but does count for this Plan).
  - Committee adjustments (Section 4.4):
    - The Committee may, in its discretion and in writing, adjust an Eligible Employee’s compensation, vesting service, or other factors used in benefit calculations for specific employees or groups, provided no violation of Section 409A.

- Article Five (Investment of Eligible Employee Accounts)
  - Investment options mirror those available under the Investment Plan and may be implemented as hypothetical accounts, actual Company-held funds, or funds held by a Trustee of a rabbi trust; investments are directed by the Eligible Employee.
  - The Committee may impose separate rules for the Company Stock Fund (including prohibitions or limits, e.g., for Section 16(b) insiders).
  - Effective July 1, 2009, the Company Stock Fund is frozen to new deferrals and transfers in; transfers/distributions out remain permitted.
  - The Company is ultimately responsible for paying deferred amounts with earnings/losses per the Plan. A Trustee may be appointed to hold and invest accounts as directed by the Committee; absent a Trustee, the Committee maintains bookkeeping accounts and credits earnings based on Investment Plan benchmarks.

nodes.title: Investment of Eligible Employee Accounts
nodes.heading:
ARTICLE FIVE

Investment of Eligible Employee Accounts
nodes.start_phrase: The Committee shall establish the same investment options under this Plan as are available from time to time under the Investment Plan.
nodes.summary:
- Committee Adjustments (Sec. 4.4): The Committee may, in its sole discretion and with written documentation, adjust an Eligible Employee’s compensation, vesting service, or other benefit factors for Plan calculations for specific individuals or groups, provided no adjustment violates Section 409A.

- Investment of Accounts (Art. 5):
  - Plan investment options mirror those of the Investment Plan, using hypothetical tracking accounts, company-held funds, or a rabbi trust; Eligible Employees direct their investment allocations.
  - The Committee may impose independent rules on the Company Stock Fund (including prohibitions and Section 16(b) restrictions). The Company Stock Fund is frozen effective July 1, 2009 (no new deferrals/transfers in; transfers/distributions out permitted under the Plan).
  - The Company is ultimately liable for benefit payments; it may appoint a Trustee to hold and invest assets per Committee direction or maintain bookkeeping accounts benchmarking Investment Plan returns when no Trustee is appointed.
  - Company allocations (Sec. 4.2) are subject to the same investment/transfer restrictions as comparable Investment Plan contributions.
  - Rollovers: The Committee may transfer balances from other unfunded Company deferred compensation plans into this Plan for common investment, preserving original deferral elections, subject to asset-type compatibility, this Plan’s terms/trust provisions, and Section 409A.

- Creditor and Assignment Rules (Sec. 5.4–5.5):
  - Trust accounts are subject to Company creditors in insolvency; benefits are unsecured claims against a Participating Company’s general assets.
  - Benefits are non-assignable and protected from garnishment, etc., except as permitted under a Domestic Relations Order (Sec. 9.2).
  - The Plan is unfunded as of its original effective date; the Company may establish a rabbi or other grantor trust, with each Participating Company responsible for its own employees’ benefits; no employee property rights in any trust assets.

- Benefits (Art. 6):
  - Vesting (Sec. 6.1): Employee deferrals (Sec. 4.1), long-service company allocations (Sec. 4.2(b)), and related earnings are always 100% vested; company matching allocations (Sec. 4.2(a)) and earnings vest per the Investment Plan’s matching vesting rules.
  - Timing/Form of Payments (Sec. 6.2):
    - Retirement: Upon termination on/after age 55 with at least five years of vesting service, benefits are paid in cash either as a lump sum or substantially equal annual installments over five years, commencing within 60 days after the six-month anniversary of termination. The form is elected at the time of deferral; default is a lump sum if no valid election exists. Vesting service follows Investment Plan rules as of Jan 1, 2008. “Termination of employment” follows Section 409A; for qualifying medical leaves, termination is deemed after a 29-month absence.
    - Death: The account is payable to the designated beneficiary (person, trust, or estate) per the most recent written designation; prior designations are automatically revoked upon a new filing and beneficiary consent is not required. If death occurs during installment payments, the remaining balance is paid in a lump sum within 60 days after death.

nodes.title: Benefits
nodes.heading:
ARTICLE SIX

Benefits
nodes.start_phrase: An Eligible Employee’ s contributions under Section 4.1, the Company’ s allocations for long-service Eligible Employees under Section 4.2(b) and the earnings on all such contributions are 100 percent vested at all times.
nodes.summary:
- Article Six – Benefits
  - Vesting: Employee deferrals, long-service allocations, and related earnings are always 100% vested; Company matching contributions vest according to the Investment Plan’s matching vesting schedule.
  - Retirement benefits: If employment ends at or after age 55 with five years of vesting service, benefits are paid in cash as a lump sum or five substantially equal annual installments; payments begin within 60 days after the six-month anniversary of termination. Form of payment is elected at deferral; default is lump sum if no valid election. Vesting service measured under the Investment Plan as of January 1, 2008. “Termination of employment” follows Section 409A, with a special rule deeming termination after a 29-month medically based leave.
  - Death benefits: Payable to the most recently designated beneficiary (person, trust, or estate); prior designations are automatically revoked by a new one. If death occurs during installments, remaining balance is paid in a lump sum within 60 days; if before benefits start, the entire balance is paid in a lump sum within 60 days. If no valid beneficiary, payment goes to the estate.
  - Other terminations: Vested balance is paid in a single lump sum within 60 days after termination. For “specified employees,” payments are delayed six months per Section 409A, then paid within 60 days thereafter. The same 29-month medical leave rule applies to the termination definition.
  - In-service withdrawals: The Committee may approve distributions for an Unforeseeable Financial Emergency (as defined under Section 409A), limited to the vested balance or the amount necessary to meet the emergency plus related taxes, after considering insurance and reasonable asset liquidation. Emergencies include participant/spouse/dependent illness or accident, casualty loss, or other extraordinary, unforeseeable events beyond the participant’s control; determinations are at the Committee’s sole discretion.
  - Change in Control: All accounts become or remain 100% vested. The Committee may either distribute all balances in a lump sum or continue the Plan, deciding within a window from 30 days before to 180 days after the Change in Control. Any termination/liquidation must comply with Section 409A.
  - Plan mergers: Effective February 2, 2004, the CCS Supplemental Investment Plan and CCS Supplemental Retirement Plan were merged into this Plan; distributions on and after that date follow this Plan’s rules.

- Article Seven – Administration and Procedures
  - The Committee administers the Plan, informs employees of deferral, investment, and beneficiary elections, and maintains records.
  - Individual accounts are established for each Eligible Employee to track contributions, earnings/losses, and withdrawals; the Committee determines benefits and directs payment by the Company, a Participating Company, or the Trustee.
  - The Committee has sole discretionary authority to determine eligibility, benefit amounts, interpret the Plan, and adopt administrative rules; its decisions are final and conclusive. Committee members have no individual liability, and the Company indemnifies them for actions taken in their Committee roles.

nodes.title: Administration and Procedures
nodes.heading:
ARTICLE SEVEN

Administration and Pr ocedur es
nodes.start_phrase: This Plan shall be administered by the Committee in accordance with the Plan’ s terms.
nodes.summary:
- Change in Control: All Eligible Employees become 100% vested; the Committee may either distribute all accrued balances in a lump sum or allow the Plan to continue; decision window spans from 30 days before an anticipated Change in Control to 180 days after an actual Change in Control; any termination/liquidation must comply with Section 409A.
- Plan mergers: The CCS Supplemental Investment Plan and CCS Supplemental Retirement Plan were merged into this Plan effective February 2, 2004; distributions on/after that date follow this Plan’s rules.
- Administration: The Committee administers the Plan, informs employees of deferral/investment/beneficiary elections, maintains individual accounts (tracking contributions, earnings/losses, withdrawals), determines benefits, and directs payment by the Company/Participating Company/Trustee.
- Committee authority and protections: The Committee has sole discretion over eligibility, benefits, interpretation, and administrative rules; its decisions are final and conclusive; members have no personal liability, and the Company indemnifies them for Committee-related actions.
- Consistency with Investment Plan: Terms and unresolved administrative/benefit questions are interpreted consistently with the Investment Plan.
- Claims procedures: Written claims decided within 90 days (extendable by 90 with notice); denials must cite reasons and Plan provisions and explain needed information and appeal rights. Appeals must be filed within 60 days; claimants may submit additional information and access relevant documents at no charge. Appeals decided within 60 days (extendable to 120 with notice). Claimants must exhaust these procedures before litigation; any suit must be filed by the earlier of the statute of limitations or one year after the appeal decision.
- Amendment and termination: The Company may amend or terminate the Plan at any time; the Board may delegate technical amendments to a Vice President or higher; all changes must comply with Section 409A (e.g., no impermissible accelerations or added benefits).
- Company obligations: The Company contractually commits to pay accrued benefits to Eligible Employees to the extent it is financially capable.
- Miscellaneous: The Plan does not create an employment contract or guarantee continued employment; benefits are non-transferable except by will or laws of descent and distribution and are exercisable only by the employee or their legal representative; benefits may be assigned pursuant to a qualifying Domestic Relations Order (definition to be detailed; section incomplete).

nodes.title: Amendment and Termination
nodes.heading:
ARTICLE EIGHT

Amendment and Termination
nodes.start_phrase: The Company reserves the right to amend or to terminate the Plan at any time for whatever reason it may deem appropriate.
nodes.summary:
- Requires claimants to exhaust internal plan claims and appeals procedures before filing any lawsuit, and limits court actions to the earlier of the applicable statute of limitations or one year from the Committee’s appeal decision.
- Grants the Company authority to amend or terminate the plan at any time, with the Board able to delegate technical amendment authority to a Vice President-level employee, subject to Section 409A restrictions (e.g., no accelerated payments or added benefits).
- States the Company’s contractual commitment to pay accrued benefits, limited to the Company’s financial capability.
- Clarifies the plan does not create an employment contract or guarantee continued employment; participating companies may terminate employment with or without cause.
- Prohibits transfer of an employee’s plan rights during life except by will or laws of descent and distribution, and permits exercise only by the employee or their legal representative.
- Allows payment of all or part of an employee’s account to another person under an approved domestic relations order, with a definition of such orders beginning but not fully included in the excerpt.

nodes.title: Miscellaneous
nodes.heading:
ARTICLE NINE

Miscellaneous
nodes.start_phrase: Nothing contained in this Plan shall be construed as a contract of employment between the Company and an Eligible Employee, or as a right of any Eligible Employee to be continued in the employment of a Participating Company , or as a limitation of the right of a Participating Company to dischar ge any of its Eligible Employees, with or without cause.
nodes.summary:
- Requires claimants to exhaust internal claims and appeals procedures before filing suit; any court action must be brought by the earlier of the applicable statute of limitations or one year from the Committee’s appeal decision.
- Company may amend or terminate the Plan at any time; Board may delegate authority for technical amendments; all changes must comply with Section 409A (e.g., no impermissible accelerations or added benefits). Company contractually commits to pay accrued benefits to Eligible Employees to the extent financially capable.
- Clarifies employment status: the Plan does not constitute a contract of employment or guarantee of continued employment.
- Plan rights are nontransferable except by will or laws of descent and distribution; may be exercised only by the employee or legal representative.
- Allows payment to an Alternate Payee under a qualifying Domestic Relations Order that meets specified criteria (issued under state domestic relations law; relates to support/alimony/marital property; recognizes an Alternate Payee’s right; preserves value equivalence; meets Board conditions). The Board (or delegate) determines DRO status, considering Code Section 414(p) and ERISA section 206(d).
- Governing law is New York.
- Plan is governed by and administered to comply with Section 409A; conflicting provisions are interpreted/amended to maintain compliance; the Committee may take necessary actions and rely on transition rules.
- Benefits are subject to applicable federal, state, and local income and employment taxes.
- Plan binds the Company’s successors and assigns.
- Effective dates: original Plan effective January 1, 1997; second amended and restated document effective January 1, 2023; executed December 8, 2022 by John P. MacMahon, Senior Vice President – Global Compensation and Benefits.
- Restatement introduction for the Corning Incorporated Executive Supplemental Pension Plan (as amended and restated effective January 1, 2023); applies to eligible Employees retiring on or after December 6, 2006.
- Definitions include:
  - Board: Board of Directors of Corning Incorporated.
  - Change in Control: within Section 409A parameters, triggered by (i) a tender/exchange offer purchase of Corning common stock by a non-Company offeror, (ii) any person acquiring 50%+ of voting power, (iii) a contested election resulting in a majority Board turnover within 12 months, or (iv) merger where Company is not the survivor, sale of substantially all assets, or shareholder-approved partial/complete liquidation.
  - Code: Internal Revenue Code of 1986, as amended.

nodes.title: CORNING INCORPORATED EXECUTIVE SUPPLEMENTAL PENSION PLAN (As Amended and Restated Effective January 1, 2023)
nodes.heading:
Exhibit 10.41

CORNING INCORPORA TED

EXECUTIVE SUPPLEMENT AL PENSION PLAN

(As Amended and Restated Effective January 1, 2023)
nodes.start_phrase: CORNING INCORPORA TED (the “Company”) hereby amends and restates effective January 1, 2023, the Corning Incorporated Executive Supplemental Pension Plan (the “Plan”) for the benefit of eligible Employees.
nodes.summary:
- Exhibit 10.41 sets out the Corning Incorporated Executive Supplemental Pension Plan, amended and restated effective January 1, 2023.
- The restated Plan applies to eligible employees who retire on or after December 6, 2006.
- Article One provides key definitions:
  - “Board” refers to Corning Incorporated’s Board of Directors.
  - “Change in Control” follows Section 409A standards and includes:
    - A third-party tender or exchange offer for Corning common stock.
    - Any person becoming the beneficial owner of 50% or more of the Company’s voting securities (per Exchange Act Sections 13(d) and 14(d)(2)).
    - A contested election resulting in a majority turnover of the Board within a 12-month period.
    - A merger where Corning is not the survivor, a consolidation, sale or disposition of all or substantially all assets, or a shareholder-approved partial or complete liquidation.
  - “Code” means the Internal Revenue Code of 1986, as amended.

nodes.title: Definitions
nodes.heading:
ARTICLE ONE

Definitions
nodes.start_phrase: “Board” means the Board of Directors of Corning Incorporated.
nodes.summary:
- Exhibit 10.41: Corning Incorporated Executive Supplemental Pension Plan (ESPP), amended and restated effective January 1, 2023; applies to eligible employees who retire on or after December 6, 2006.
- Purpose and intent: Provide supplemental retirement benefits beyond limits of the Qualified Plan to attract and retain executives; designed as an unfunded deferred compensation “top hat” plan for a select group of management or highly compensated employees under ERISA; intended to comply with IRC Section 409A; plan terms supersede any inconsistent prior plans/documents.
- Key definitions:
  - Board: Board of Directors of Corning Incorporated.
  - Committee: Compensation Committee of the Board or its delegate.
  - Company: Corning Incorporated.
  - Employee: An employee of a Participating Company who participates in the Qualified Plan and is management or highly compensated under ERISA.
  - Participating Company: The Company and related entities meeting the Qualified Plan’s “Company” definition and approved by the Committee.
  - Plan: This Executive Supplemental Pension Plan.
  - Qualified Plan: The Corning Incorporated Pension Plan for Salaried Employees.
  - Code and Section 409A: Internal Revenue Code and related 409A regulations/guidance.
  - Normal Retirement Date: First day of the month following the later of age 65 or five vesting years of service.
  - Total and Permanent Disability: Inability to engage in substantial gainful activity due to a long-term/indefinite impairment, as determined by the Committee.
  - Change in Control: As defined under Section 409A and includes any of the following—(i) third-party tender or exchange offer for Corning common stock; (ii) a person becomes beneficial owner of 50%+ of voting power; (iii) within 12 months, a majority of directors are elected via contested elections; or (iv) a merger where Corning is not the survivor, consolidation, sale of all/substantially all assets, or shareholder-approved partial/complete liquidation.

nodes.title: Purpose and Intent of Plan
nodes.heading:
ARTICLE TWO

Purpose and Intent of Plan
nodes.start_phrase: The purpose of this Plan is to attract and retain a highly-motivated executive workforce by providing to eligible Employees retirement benefits in excess of those permitted under the Qualified Plan.
nodes.summary:
- Establishes key definitions for the plan, including Committee (Compensation Committee or its delegate), Company (Corning Incorporated), Employee (participants in the Qualified Plan who are management or highly compensated under ERISA Title I), Normal Retirement Date (first day of the month after age 65 and five vesting years), Participating Company, Plan, Qualified Plan, Section 409A, and Total and Permanent Disability.
- States the plan’s purpose: to attract and retain executives by providing retirement benefits above those allowed under the Qualified Plan; intended as an unfunded “top-hat” deferred compensation plan for a select group under ERISA Title I; to be administered in compliance with Section 409A; and to supersede conflicting or additional terms in other documents.
- Provides eligibility rules: the Committee has sole discretion to designate eligible Employees and maintain related records.
- Details disqualification and forfeiture conditions: an otherwise eligible Employee is ineligible if terminated for cause; violates noncompete/confidentiality or similar agreements; solicits Company employees; works for or serves a third party (including competitors) in a way the Committee deems harmful; or files/threatens legal action (including patent claims) deemed harmful. Violations of these conditions can result in forfeiture of future benefits and repayment of benefits already paid, at the Committee’s sole discretion.
- Clarifies coordination with other plans: participants in this plan are not entitled to benefits under the Corning Incorporated Supplemental Pension Plan.
- Introduces the Benefits section (Article Four) and references a Benefit Amount provision, though the specific benefit formula/details are not included in the excerpt.

nodes.title: Eligible Employee
nodes.heading:
ARTICLE THREE

Eligible Employee
nodes.start_phrase: The Committee, in its sole discretion, shall designate those Employees who shall be eligible to participate in this Plan.

nodes.title: Benefits
nodes.heading:
ARTICLE FOUR

Benefits
nodes.start_phrase: The benefit payable under this Plan is, as follows:
nodes.summary:
- Article Three – Eligible Employee:
  - Eligibility is determined solely by the Committee, which maintains official records.
  - Disqualifying conduct results in ineligibility and forfeiture, including: termination for cause; violating noncompete/confidentiality; soliciting employees; working for or serving third parties that may harm the Company; filing or threatening legal action (e.g., patent claims) deemed harmful. For violations (b–e), future benefits are forfeited and previously paid benefits must be repaid.
  - Employees eligible under this Plan are not entitled to benefits under the Corning Incorporated Supplemental Pension Plan (SPP).

- Article Four – Benefits:
  - 4.1 Benefit Amount:
    - A (general participants; excludes Exhibit A):
      - Vesting: terminate after reaching age 50 and 10 years of Credited Service, or grandfathered if age 55 by 12/5/2006 and age+service ≥ 65. If not vested, see 4.1C.
      - Formula at Normal Retirement Date: 2% × Credited Service (max 25 years) × Average Compensation, minus the actual Qualified Plan benefit. Compensation and Average Compensation defined with detailed inclusions/exclusions; Committee may expand includable pay. When offsetting by the Qualified Plan, Career Average Contributions and related interest credited on/after 1/1/2023 are ignored.
      - Early retirement: unreduced if separate at 55 with 25 years of service or at 60 with 10 years. Otherwise: reduction of 1/3% per month before age 60; disability gets unreduced benefit; separation before 55 begins after 55 with a 50% reduction. Special rules apply if the straight life annuity at Normal Retirement Date exceeds 4× the 401(a)(17) limit, including different unreduced triggers and a 1/12% per month reduction to age 57 for certain cases.
    - B (Exhibit A participants):
      - Fully vested. Formula: 1.5% × Credited Service × Average Compensation, minus the Qualified Plan benefit. Same compensation, service, averaging rules; post‑2022 Career Average Contributions and interest ignored in the offset.
      - Early retirement rules mirror Section A (unreduced at 55/25 or 60/10; otherwise 1/3% per month to 60; disability unreduced; 50% reduction if separating before 55).
    - C (for those not vested under 4.1A):
      - Benefit equals what would be payable under the SPP formula and terms (including vesting), paid as a lump sum within 60 days after the first of the month following separation from service per SPP Section 4.3.
    - D:
      - The Committee may adjust an individual’s compensation, credited service, or other calculation factors at its discretion, documented in writing.
  - 4.2 Commencement:
    - Payments start within 60 days after the first of the month following the later of separation from service (Section 409A) or age 55. “Specified employees” face a six‑month delay, with suspended amounts paid in a lump sum at the start of month seven.
  - 4.3 Form of Payment:
    - Default: life annuity (unmarried) or joint and 75% survivor annuity (married). Optional forms: single life or joint and 50/75/100% survivor. All are actuarially equivalent; annuities paid as six‑year certain with no extra adjustment for the six‑year certain feature.
    - Special rules:
      - Frozen Cash Balance SPP Benefit (accrued before participation here) is paid as a lump sum at separation; the Plan’s annuity is offset by its value. Interest crediting and conversion to an annuity for offset use 417(e)(3) rates/tables set as of entry into this Plan (with 12/31/2008 locking for certain participants).
      - Benefits under 4.6 (Change in Control) and small benefits (<$20,000) are paid as lump sums using 417(e)(3) assumptions.
      - For the individual on Exhibit B, the Company will purchase a MetLife annuity post‑separation.
  - 4.4 Death Benefits:
    - If death occurs while employed, vested, and age 55 or older: surviving spouse receives 100% of the benefit as if begun at death; starts within 60 days after the first of the month following death. If spouse >5 years younger, a 0.2% per month reduction applies based on the age difference metric provided.
    - If death occurs while employed, vested, and before 55: spouse receives 50% of the Normal Retirement Date benefit; similar timing and age‑difference reduction.
    - If separated before 55, vested, and die before commencement: spouse receives 50% of the Normal Retirement Date benefit reduced by 50%, starting within 60 days after the first of the month the employee would reach 55; similar age‑difference reduction.
    - Any Frozen Cash Balance SPP Benefit is paid as a lump sum to the beneficiary within 60 days of death; other death benefits are offset by its value using the stated methodology.
  - 4.5 Unfunded Plan:
    - Benefits are paid from the general assets of the employing Participating Company; the Plan is unfunded though the Company may establish a rabbi or similar trust. Rights are unsecured claims.
  - 4.6 Change in Control:
    - All eligible Employees become fully vested using Section 4.1A (Exhibit A uses 4.1B), assuming unreduced early retirement eligibility. If separation occurs within 12 months of the Change in Control, payment is a lump sum within 60 days after the first of the month of separation (subject to 409A six‑month delay for specified employees). Those under 55 receive the present value of the benefit payable at 55 based on compensation and service at termination. Forfeiture rules in Section 3.1 still apply.

- Article Five – Administration:
  - The Committee administers the Plan, determines benefits, directs payment by the Qualified Plan or Participating Company, informs employees of elections, and maintains records.
  - Interpretation aligns with the Qualified Plan; undefined issues or terms default to the Qualified Plan unless context requires otherwise.

nodes.title: Administration
nodes.heading:
ARTICLE FIVE

Administration
nodes.start_phrase: This Plan shall be administered by the Committee in accordance with the Plan’ s terms.
nodes.summary:
- Plan funding and security: Benefits are unfunded and paid from the employing Participating Company’s general assets. The Company may, at its discretion, set aside assets (e.g., a rabbi or other grantor trust), with each Participating Company funding benefits for its own employees. Employees have no property rights in any such assets; benefits are unsecured general creditor claims.

- Change in Control protections: Upon a Change in Control (subject to any forfeiture in Section 3.1), eligible employees become fully vested using Section 4.1A (or 4.1B for those on Exhibit A), assuming eligibility for an unreduced early retirement benefit. If a Section 409A “separation from service” occurs within 12 months, benefits are paid as a single lump sum within 60 days of the first of the month following separation, subject to any six-month delay. Employees under age 55 receive an immediate lump sum equal to the present value of the benefit payable at age 55, based on compensation and credited service at termination.

- Administration and authority: A Committee administers the Plan, determines eligibility and benefit amounts, coordinates payments with the Qualified Plan or Participating Companies, informs employees of elections, and interprets the Plan. Its decisions are final and conclusive. Committee members are indemnified by the Company and not individually liable. Plan terms and interpretations align with the Qualified Plan unless context dictates otherwise.

- Claims and appeals: Claims must be submitted in writing. Initial decisions are generally issued within 90 days (with one 90-day extension upon notice). Denial notices provide reasons, Plan citations, needed additional information, and appeal procedures. Appeals must be filed within 60 days, with the right to submit additional materials and obtain relevant documents at no cost. Appeals are decided within 60 days (extendable with notice, but no later than 120 days from receipt). Claimants must exhaust these procedures before filing suit; any action must be brought by the earlier of the applicable statute of limitations or one year from the appeal decision.

- Amendment and termination: The Board may amend or terminate the Plan at any time (technical amendments may be delegated to a Vice President or higher), subject to Section 409A compliance. The Company commits, on behalf of itself and other Participating Companies and their successors, to pay accrued benefits earned before amendment or termination to the extent financially capable.

- Employment status: The Plan does not create an employment contract, guarantee continued employment, or limit a Participating Company’s right to discharge employees.

nodes.title: Amendment and Termination
nodes.heading:
ARTICLE SIX

Amendment and Termination
nodes.start_phrase: While the Company intends to maintain this Plan in conjunction with the Qualified Plan indefinitely , the Board reserves the right to amend or terminate it at any time for whatever reasons it may deem appropriate.
nodes.summary:
- Appeal decisions will generally be issued within 60 days of receipt; extensions are allowed for special circumstances with prior written notice, not to exceed 120 days total.
- Adverse decision notices must state reasons, cite specific Plan provisions, and inform claimants of their right to free access to relevant documents and records.
- Claimants must exhaust the Plan’s claims and appeal procedures before filing suit. Any court action must be filed by the earlier of the applicable statute of limitations or one year from the Committee’s appeal decision.
- Amendment and Termination: The Board may amend or terminate the Plan at any time and may delegate technical amendments to a Vice President or higher, with all changes complying with Section 409A.
- The Company commits, for itself and Participating Companies, to pay benefits accrued before any amendment or termination to the extent they are financially able.
- Miscellaneous: The Plan does not create an employment contract or guarantee continued employment; Participating Companies may discharge employees with or without cause.

nodes.title: Miscellaneous
nodes.heading:
ARTICLE SEVEN

Miscellaneous
nodes.start_phrase: Nothing contained in this Plan shall be construed as a contract of employm ent between a Participating Company and an Employee, or as a right of any Employee to be continued in the employment of a Participating Company , or as a limitation of the right of a Participating Company to dischar ge any of its Employees, with or without cause.
nodes.summary:
- Claims and appeals: The Committee generally decides appeals within 60 days; extensions require advance written notice, special-circumstances explanation, and a decision no later than 120 days. Adverse decisions must state reasons, cite specific Plan provisions, and inform claimants of their right to free access to relevant documents.
- Exhaustion and litigation limits: Claimants must exhaust Plan claims procedures before filing suit. Any court action to review an adverse appeal decision must be filed by the earlier of the applicable statute of limitations or one year from the Committee’s appeal decision.
- Amendment and termination: The Board may amend or terminate the Plan at any time (technical amendments may be delegated to a Vice President), subject to Section 409A compliance. The Company commits to pay accrued benefits earned before any amendment/termination to the extent financially capable.
- Employment status: Participation does not create a contract of employment or limit the employer’s right to terminate employment.
- Non‑transferability: Benefits are non-assignable except by will or laws of descent and distribution; rights are exercisable only by the employee or legal representative.
- Domestic Relations Orders: The Plan may pay all or part of a benefit to an Alternate Payee pursuant to a qualifying domestic relations order that: is issued under state domestic relations law; relates to child support, alimony, or marital property; recognizes an Alternate Payee’s right to Plan benefits; preserves value without accelerating payment; and meets Board‑established requirements. The Board (or delegate) determines qualification and may apply Code Section 414(p) and ERISA Section 206(d) standards.
- Taxation: Benefits are subject to applicable federal, state, and local income and employment taxes.
- Indemnification: The Company will indemnify eligible employees for actions/proceedings related to Plan nonpayment or anticipated nonperformance (including fees and costs), with advancement subject to repayment if ultimately not entitled. Reimbursements must be made by year‑end of expense or by the 15th day of the third month after incurrence, upon timely documentation. No indemnification if participation ceases and benefits are forfeited for cause or noncompete violations.
- Successors: The Plan binds the Company’s successors and assigns.
- Section 409A: The Plan is governed by, and will be interpreted to comply with, Section 409A; the Committee may take actions to ensure compliance and apply transition rules. 2007 amendments affecting time/form of payment are limited to amounts not otherwise payable in 2007.
- Effective dates: Original effective date January 1, 1986; second restatement effective January 1, 2023; terms apply to employees retiring on/after December 6, 2006. 409A‑related provisions effective January 1, 2005; specified employees’ six‑month delay applied only to amounts earned/vested after December 31, 2004.
- Governing law: New York.
- Execution: Signed December 8, 2022, by Corning Incorporated’s Senior Vice President – Global Compensation and Benefits.
- Exhibits: Exhibit A and Exhibit B list named individuals.
- Beginning of restated Plan text (Exhibit 10.42): States the Plan is amended and restated effective January 1, 2023, applying to benefits earned/vested on or after January 1, 2005; includes definitions such as “Board” and “Change in Control” (aligned with Section 409A) with triggers including a tender/exchange offer, acquisition of 50%+ voting power, contested Board turnover within 12 months, and merger/sale/liquidation transactions where the Company is not the survivor or sells substantially all assets.

nodes.title: CORNING INCORPORATED SUPPLEMENTAL PENSION PLAN (As Amended and Restated Effective January 1, 2023)
nodes.heading:
Exhibit 10.42

CORNING INCORPORA TED

SUPPLEMENT AL PENSION PLAN

(As Amended and Restated Effective January 1, 2023)
nodes.start_phrase: CORNING INCORPORA TED (the “Company”) hereby amends and restates effective January 1, 2023, the Corning Incorporated Supplemental Pension Plan (the Plan”) for the benefit of eligible Employees.
nodes.summary:
- Exhibit 10.42 outlines the Corning Incorporated Supplemental Pension Plan, amended and restated effective January 1, 2023.
- The restated plan applies to eligible employees with benefits earned or vested (within the meaning of Section 409A) on or after January 1, 2005.
- Article One (Definitions) includes:
  - “Board” defined as the Board of Directors of Corning Incorporated.
  - “Change in Control” defined consistent with Section 409A and triggered by:
    - A third party purchasing Corning common stock via a tender or exchange offer.
    - Any person becoming the beneficial owner of 50% or more of the combined voting power of the company’s outstanding securities.
    - A contested election resulting in a majority board turnover within a 12-month period.
    - A merger where Corning is not the surviving corporation, a consolidation, a sale/disposition of all or substantially all assets, or a shareholder-approved partial or complete liquidation.

nodes.title: Definitions
nodes.heading:
ARTICLE ONE

Definitions
nodes.start_phrase: “Board” means the Board of Directors of Corning Incorporated.
nodes.summary:
- Exhibit 10.42: Corning Incorporated Supplemental Pension Plan, amended and restated effective January 1, 2023.
- Applicability: Applies to eligible employees with benefits earned or vested (as defined under Section 409A) on or after January 1, 2005.
- Article One—Definitions:
  - Board: Board of Directors of Corning Incorporated.
  - Change in Control: Defined consistent with Section 409A and includes any of the following: (i) a third-party tender or exchange offer for Corning stock; (ii) a person becoming the beneficial owner of 50%+ of combined voting power; (iii) a contested election resulting in a majority board turnover within 12 months; (iv) a merger where Corning is not the survivor, consolidation, sale of all or substantially all assets, or a shareholder-approved partial/complete liquidation.
  - Code: Internal Revenue Code of 1986.
  - Committee: Compensation Committee of the Board or its delegate.
  - Company: Corning Incorporated.
  - Employee: An employee of a Participating Company who participates in the Qualified Plan and is management or highly compensated under ERISA Title I.
  - Normal/Early Retirement Date: As defined in the Qualified Plan.
  - Participating Company: The Company or related entities that meet the Qualified Plan’s “Company” definition and are approved by the Committee.
  - Plan: This Supplemental Pension Plan.
  - Qualified Plan: The Corning Incorporated Pension Plan for Salaried Employees.
  - Section 409A: Code Section 409A and related guidance.
- Article Two—Purpose and Intent:
  - Purpose: Attract and retain a highly motivated executive workforce by providing retirement benefits in excess of Qualified Plan limits.
  - Plan status: An unfunded deferred compensation plan for a select group of management or highly compensated employees (ERISA “top-hat” plan).
  - Compliance: Intended to comply with Section 409A and to be interpreted accordingly.
  - Supersession: Plan terms supersede any inconsistent or additional terms in other plans/documents.
- Article Three—Eligibility:
  - Begins listing categories of employees eligible to participate (details not fully included in the excerpt).

nodes.title: Purpose and Intent of Plan
nodes.heading:
ARTICLE TWO

Purpose and Intent of Plan
nodes.start_phrase: The purpose of this Plan is to attract and retain a highly-motivated executive workforce by providing to eligible Employees retirement benefits in excess of those permitted under the Qualified Plan.
nodes.summary: The excerpt defines key terms for the Corning Incorporated Supplemental Pension Plan, including Code (Internal Revenue Code), Committee (Compensation Committee or its delegate), Company (Corning Incorporated), Employee (management or highly compensated employees who participate in the Qualified Plan), Normal/Early Retirement Date (as defined in the Qualified Plan), Participating Company (entities meeting the Qualified Plan’s “Company” definition and approved by the Committee), Plan (this supplemental plan), Qualified Plan (The Corning Incorporated Pension Plan for Salaried Employees), and Section 409A (and its regulations). It outlines the plan’s purpose: to attract and retain executives by providing supplemental retirement benefits beyond Qualified Plan limits, structured as an unfunded deferred compensation “top-hat” plan under ERISA Title I and intended to comply with Section 409A, with its terms superseding any inconsistent documents. The Eligibility article begins, indicating categories of eligible employees will be specified (details not included in the excerpt).

nodes.title: Eligibility
nodes.heading:
ARTICLE THREE

Eligibility
nodes.start_phrase: The following categories of Employees are eligible to participate in this Plan:
nodes.summary:
- Defines key terms used in the plan: Code (Internal Revenue Code), Committee (Compensation Committee or its delegate), Company (Corning Incorporated), Employee (participants in the Qualified Plan who are management or highly compensated under ERISA Title I), Normal/Early Retirement Date (as in the Qualified Plan), Participating Company (Company and related entities approved by the Committee), Plan (this Supplemental Pension Plan), Qualified Plan (The Corning Incorporated Pension Plan for Salaried Employees), and Section 409A (and related guidance).
- States the plan’s purpose and intent: to attract and retain a highly motivated executive workforce by providing supplemental retirement benefits beyond limits of the Qualified Plan; to operate as an unfunded “top-hat” plan for a select group of management or highly compensated employees under ERISA Title I; and to comply with Section 409A. The plan’s terms supersede any inconsistent documents.
- Outlines eligibility:
  - Eligible: employees whose Qualified Plan benefits are limited by Code Section 415, the compensation cap of Section 401(a)(17), or other Code limits; and any other employees designated by the Committee (with the Committee maintaining records).
  - Ineligible/forfeiture: employees terminated for cause (as determined by the Committee) or those who terminate employment before becoming fully vested in the Qualified Plan.
  - Coordination rule: employees designated for the Executive Supplemental Pension Plan receive no benefits under this plan; their benefits are determined under the executive plan, which generally preserves vested accruals from this plan up to the switch date.
- Begins the benefits section:
  - For employees with a Part I career average benefit under the Qualified Plan, the supplemental benefit payable at Normal or Early Retirement is a straight life annuity equal to the excess of the benefit computed under the Qualified Plan’s Part I formula without Code-related limits (with specified modifications) over the capped Qualified Plan benefit. The text references Section 4.2 for benefit commencement and is cut off mid-formula.

nodes.title: Benefits
nodes.heading:
ARTICLE FOUR

Benefits
nodes.start_phrase: For an eligible Employee entitled to a Part I career average benefit under the Qualified Plan, the supplemental career average benefit payable under this Plan on his or her Normal or Early Retireme nt Date shall be a straight life annuity equal to the excess of (i) over (ii) where:
nodes.summary:
- Purpose and scope: Supplemental, nonqualified pension plan intended to make up benefits limited under the company’s tax‑qualified pension plan (Qualified Plan), covering both Part I career average and Part II cash balance formulas.

- Eligibility and exclusions:
  - Eligible: Employees whose Qualified Plan benefits are limited by Code Sections 415, 401(a)(17), or other Code limits; and any other employees designated by the Committee.
  - Ineligible/forfeiture: Employees terminated for cause (Committee’s sole discretion) or who leave before becoming fully vested in the Qualified Plan.
  - Coordination with Executive Supplemental Pension Plan: Employees designated for that plan are not eligible here; their vested accrued benefits under this plan are ensured under the executive plan’s terms when participation begins.

- Benefit formulas (supplemental amounts equal the excess over what the Qualified Plan actually pays):
  - Part I career average: Paid as an annuity; equals the Qualified Plan Part I benefit without Code limits (with stated modifications) minus the actual Qualified Plan Part I benefit.
  - Part II cash balance: Paid as a lump sum; equals the Qualified Plan Part II amount without Code limits (with stated modifications) minus the actual Qualified Plan Part II amount.

- Key modifications for calculations:
  - Compensation definition expanded to include specified cash awards/bonuses and to exclude certain items (e.g., stock awards, non-cash bonuses, severance); Committee may include additional compensatory items.
  - With Committee approval, service may include prior employer service for those retiring at/after age 55.
  - Committee may substitute a minimum dollar or percent‑of‑pay benefit, offset by the Qualified Plan benefit.
  - For Part II: Career Average Contributions and related Interest Allocations effective January 1, 2023 are disregarded so no supplemental amount is paid or reduced for those credits.

- General calculation rules:
  - Otherwise mirror the Qualified Plan, including early retirement reductions and defined terms.
  - Part II supplemental benefit is based on the stated cash balance account without applying tax‑qualification rules not embedded in the Qualified Plan formula.
  - Disability‑based special adjustments under the Qualified Plan do not apply here after termination.

- Committee adjustment authority (Section 4.2): Committee may adjust compensation, credited/vesting service, or other factors for any specified employee(s), with written documentation.

- Benefit commencement (Section 4.3):
  - Part I: Start within 60 days of the first of the month following the later of separation from service (Section 409A definition) or age 55.
  - Part II: Start within 60 days of the first of the month following separation from service.
  - Special 409A disability leave rule: separation deemed on the day after a 29‑month medically‑based leave.
  - 409A six‑month delay for specified employees applies (except for death payments), with catch‑up lump sum in month 7.

- Forms of payment (Section 4.4):
  - Part I: Default life annuity (unmarried) or joint & 75% survivor annuity (married); elective forms include single life or joint & 50/75/100% survivor, all actuarially equivalent. If termination after age 55 with >5 vesting years, benefit paid as a six‑year certain form per the Qualified Plan, without actuarial adjustment.
  - Part II: Lump sum only.
  - Special cashout rules: 
    - Change in control/severance payouts use Code 417(e)(3) rates/tables.
    - If the lump sum value of a Part I benefit (or related death benefit) is under $20,000, pay as a lump sum using 417(e)(3) assumptions.

- Death benefits (Section 4.5):
  - Part I: If vested employee dies before 55 while employed, surviving spouse gets a lifetime annuity equal to 50% of the employee’s Section 4.1 benefit at Normal Retirement Age (reduced if spouse is >5 years younger). If other timing applies, spouse receives the amount as if the employee terminated at death, survived to 55, elected J&S 50%, and died immediately.
  - Part II: Unpaid supplemental cash balance benefit is paid in a lump sum to the designated beneficiary within 60 days of the first of the month of death.

- Funding status (Section 4.6): Unfunded, paid from general assets; company may establish a rabbi/grantor trust. Benefits are unsecured general obligations; employees have no property rights in any trust/assets.

- Change in Control (Section 4.7):
  - Immediate full vesting (still subject to forfeiture for cause).
  - If separation from service occurs within 12 months, pay vested benefit as a lump sum within 60 days of the first of the month following separation (subject to any 409A six‑month delay).
  - If under age 55, pay the present value of the benefit that would have been payable at age 55 based on compensation and credited service at separation.

- Special “Avanex Deal” enhanced benefits (Section 4.8):
  - Eligibility: Designated “Transferred Corning Employees” under the Avanex Asset Purchase Agreement, covered by grandfathered Part I as applicable, and with age + vesting years ≥69 by 12/31/2003.
  - Early Part I commencement: Immediate benefit upon separation even if under 55; calculated as if age 55, then actuarially reduced for earlier start. Offsets apply when Qualified Plan benefits commence.
  - Rehire rules: If rehired and left Avanex before 1/31/2004, enhanced benefit is forfeited; if after that date, enhanced benefit is preserved only for pre‑Avanex service.
  - Enhanced Part II interest: Additional interest credit equal to 4% times whole years between end of post‑paid‑leave employment and earlier of age 60 or 30 vesting years, capped at 20%.

- Beneficiary designations (Section 4.9): Employees may designate beneficiaries under Committee rules; no spousal consent requirement. If none, benefits go to surviving spouse, or estate if no spouse.

- Administration (Article Five):
  - Committee administers the plan, determines eligibility and benefit amounts, maintains records, and communicates elections.
  - Interpretations and undefined matters align with the Qualified Plan; terms carry the same meanings unless context dictates otherwise.
  - Committee decisions are final and conclusive; members have no individual liability, and the company provides indemnification.

nodes.title: Administration
nodes.heading:
ARTICLE FIVE

Administration
nodes.start_phrase: This Plan shall be administered by the Committee in accordance with the Plan’ s terms.
nodes.summary:
- Enhanced Part II Benefits: For a Transferred Corning Employee with a benefit based on the Qualified Plan’s Part II cash balance formula, the Cash Balance Account receives an additional interest credit equal to 4% times the number of whole years from the end of employment (following a paid leave) to the earlier of age 60 or 30 Vesting Years of Service; capped at 20%. This is in addition to the normal interest under Qualified Plan Section 4.16(c).
- Beneficiary designations: Employees may designate beneficiaries under Committee rules; Qualified Plan spousal consent does not apply. If no designation is made, the beneficiary is the Surviving Spouse (as defined in the Qualified Plan) or, if none, the employee’s estate.
- Plan administration: The Committee administers the Plan, determines benefits under this Plan and the Qualified Plan, arranges for payments, informs employees of elections, and maintains necessary records.
- Consistency with Qualified Plan: Undefined administrative or benefit-calculation issues are resolved in light of the Qualified Plan; terms generally have the same meanings as in the Qualified Plan.
- Committee authority and finality: The Committee has sole discretion over eligibility, benefit amounts, and Plan interpretation; its decisions are final and conclusive. Committee members are not individually liable; the Company will indemnify them for actions related to their Committee duties.
- Claims procedures: 
  - Initial claim must be in writing; decision generally within 90 days, extendable once for 90 days with written notice.
  - If denied, the notice states reasons, cites Plan provisions, indicates needed additional information, and explains appeal rights and deadlines.
  - Appeals must be filed within 60 days; claimants may submit additional materials and access relevant documents free of charge.
  - Appeal decisions generally within 60 days; may be extended with notice, but not beyond 120 days from receipt of appeal. Adverse appeal decisions include reasons, citations, and document-access rights.
  - Judicial action is permitted only after exhausting these procedures and must be filed by the earlier of the applicable statute of limitations or one year from the appeal decision.
- Amendment and termination: The Board may amend or terminate the Plan at any time (VP-level designee may make technical amendments), subject to Section 409A. The Company commits to pay benefits accrued before amendment/termination to the extent financially capable.
- Miscellaneous: 
  - No employment contract or guarantee of continued employment; employers retain the right to discharge with or without cause.
  - Benefits are non-transferable except by will or laws of descent and distribution; rights are exercisable during life only by the employee or their guardian/legal representative.

nodes.title: Amendment and Termination
nodes.heading:
ARTICLE SIX

Amendment and Termination
nodes.start_phrase: While the Company intends to maintain this Plan in conjunction with the Qualified Plan indefinitely , the Board reserves the right to amend or terminate it at any time for whatever reasons it may deem appropriate.
nodes.summary:
- Claims and legal action: Participants must fully exhaust the Plan’s internal claims and appeals procedures before filing suit. After an adverse appeal decision, any court action must be filed by the earlier of the applicable statute of limitations or one year from the Committee’s appeal decision.
- Amendment and termination: The Board may amend or terminate the Plan at any time and may delegate technical amendment authority to a Company employee at least at the Vice President level. All changes must comply with Section 409A. Despite this flexibility, the Company commits (on behalf of itself, Participating Companies, and successors) to pay benefits accrued before any amendment or termination, to the extent financially able.
- No employment contract: The Plan does not create an employment contract, guarantee continued employment, or limit a Participating Company’s right to discharge employees with or without cause.
- Non-transferability: Employee rights under the Plan are non-assignable, whether voluntarily or involuntarily, except by will or laws of descent and distribution, and may be exercised during life only by the employee or their guardian/legal representative.

nodes.title: Miscellaneous
nodes.heading:
ARTICLE SEVEN

Miscellaneous
nodes.start_phrase: Nothing contained in this Plan shall be construed as a contract of employment between a Participating Company and an Employee, or as a right of any Employee to be continued in the employment of a Participating Company , or as a limitation of the right of a Participating Company to dischar ge any of its Employees, with or without cause.
nodes.summary:
- Requires claimants to exhaust the Plan’s internal claims and appeals procedures before filing suit; any court action must be brought by the earlier of the applicable statute of limitations or one year from the Committee’s appeal decision.
- Amendment and termination: The Board may amend or terminate the Plan at any time (with technical amendments delegable to a Vice President or higher), subject to Section 409A compliance; the Company commits to pay benefits accrued before any amendment/termination to the extent financially able.
- Employment status: The Plan does not create a contract of employment or guarantee continued employment; employers may terminate employment with or without cause.
- Non‑transferability: Participant rights are non‑assignable except by will or laws of descent and distribution; exercisable only by the participant or legal representative.
- Domestic Relations Orders: Benefits may be paid to an Alternate Payee under a qualifying order issued under state domestic relations law for support/alimony/marital property, that preserves value without accelerating payment and meets Board‑set requirements; the Board (or delegate) determines qualification, considering IRC §414(p) and ERISA §206(d).
- Governing law: State of New York.
- Section 409A: The Plan is administered to comply with §409A; conflicting provisions are interpreted or deemed amended to comply; the Committee may take actions/use transition rules; 2007 amendments on time/form of payment are limited to amounts not otherwise payable in 2007 and cannot cause 2007 payments not otherwise due.
- Taxation: Benefits are subject to applicable federal, state, and local income and employment taxes.
- Successors: The Plan binds the Company’s successors and assigns.
- Effective dates and execution: Original effective date January 1, 1994; second restatement effective January 1, 2023; executed December 8, 2022 by Corning Incorporated, signed by John P. MacMahon, Senior Vice President – Global Compensation and Benefits.
